text: Enhedu asked.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: I don't think dead is the right word.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik stepped closer.
speaker: Narrator

text: The figure's head turned while the rest of its body remained locked in the stone. The motion was exact, mechanical, as if the joint had been waiting centuries for the correct pressure. Empty sockets regarded him. The mouth opened.
speaker: Narrator

text: No sound came out.
speaker: Narrator

text: Instead the mark on Zik's palm flared hot, and a single word formed behind his eyes—not spoken, not written, simply present.
speaker: Narrator

text: Payment.
speaker: The City
note: A word formed behind his eyes; not spoken. The City speaking: not fully human. Whispered, wet, close.

text: He stepped back.
speaker: Narrator

text: The figure remained motionless, head still turned toward him, waiting.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag's voice was very quiet.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: What does it want?
speaker: Balag

text: Ninsun answered without looking away from the stone face.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: The same thing the tablets said every threshold wants. Something that cannot be bought back.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik looked down at his marked hand, then at the incomplete spirals carved into the walls around the plaza, then at the journal pressed against his ribs.
speaker: Narrator

text: The city had let them in.
speaker: Narrator

text: Now it was waiting to see what they would leave behind.
speaker: Narrator

text: They left the plaza without touching the gatekeeper again.
speaker: Narrator

text: The figure remained exactly as they had found it—head turned, empty sockets fixed on the space Zik had occupied, black bead resting against stone that had once been a neck. It did not follow. It did not need to. The word Payment still sat behind Zik's eyes like a coin that refused to be spent.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag took the lead, axe ready, moving as if the streets themselves might decide to close. Enhedu walked slightly apart, eyes cataloguing every doorway, every erased name, every place a valuable object might once have been. Ninsun kept close to Zik, parchment and stylus ready, though she had not written anything since the courtyard repeated itself for the third time.
speaker: Narrator

text: The street they chose ran straight for nearly a hundred paces before it simply ended.
speaker: Narrator

text: Not in a wall. Not in a collapsed building. The paving continued for three more stones and then became blank stone floor, seamless and unmarked, as if the street had never been intended to go farther. On either side the buildings leaned inward until their upper stories nearly touched, forming a tunnel of shadow that smelled of old water and something metallic.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik stopped.
speaker: Narrator

text: This wasn't here a moment ago.
speaker: Zik

text: Ninsun checked her notes, then the walls, then the incomplete spiral carved at what should have been the next intersection.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: It was. Or a different version of it was. The symbol has changed orientation.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Balag tested the blank floor with the butt of his axe. The stone gave back a dull, solid sound.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Dead end.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu was already examining the nearest doorway. The lintel above it had once carried a name. Only three characters remained, the rest gouged out so deeply that the stone itself looked wounded.
speaker: Narrator

text: Someone wanted these people forgotten,
speaker: Enhedu

text: she said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: Or the people wanted to be forgotten,
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun answered.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: In some of the older tablets, voluntary erasure is listed as a form of payment. A way to pass a threshold without losing something more essential. One damaged account claims that once a name was taken, no one who had known the person could speak it again. The word simply would not form.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik looked at the incomplete spiral on the wall. The missing section felt deliberate, like a blank space left for a signature.
speaker: Narrator

text: He opened the journal.
speaker: Narrator

text: The map had shifted again. The dense network of streets now showed a single clear path leading away from the plaza they had just left. The path ended at a mark that was not a spiral. It was a simple vertical line descending into a small open circle.
speaker: Narrator

text: Beneath it, new writing had appeared in a hand that was neither his father's nor his own.
speaker: Narrator

text: THE STREET IS A THRESHOLD.
speaker: Narrator
note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

text: CROSSING IT REQUIRES A NAME.
speaker: Narrator
note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

text: Zik closed the book. This time he did not try to hide the act. The others had seen him look.
speaker: Narrator

text: What does it say?
speaker: Ninsun

text: Ninsun asked.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: He told them.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag's expression hardened.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: We're not giving it names.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu tilted her head.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: What if it already has them?
speaker: Enhedu

text: No one answered.
speaker: Narrator

text: They stood at the edge of the blank floor for a long time. The air in the unfinished tunnel felt colder than the rest of the City. Torchlight sank into the stone and did not return. Somewhere far behind them, back toward the plaza, a single measured knock sounded—soft, almost polite.
speaker: Narrator
